_schema: The biggest single mass in most builds, and the only source of voltage sag. Two tiers, as in frames.json, motors.json and propellers.json: `specs` is physics-bearing and `catalog` is browsing metadata only — a field is admitted to `catalog` only if it is a factual, checkable property of the real product AND is needed to navigate the catalog at scale. Colour, price and vendor links are banned by name, from either block. 'cells' sets pack voltage, which sets the RPM ceiling (max_RPM = KV * live voltage) — this is most of why a 4S->6S swap feels dramatic rather than cosmetic. 'internal_r_ohm' is what makes that voltage live rather than fixed: punch the throttle, current spikes, voltage drops, RPM ceiling drops, thrust drops. 'chemistry' sits in `specs` rather than in `catalog` even though it reads like browsing metadata, because it is physics-bearing: it selects which open-circuit discharge curve BatteryModel runs (physics.md §5), and a LiPo and a Li-ion at the same state of charge do not rest at the same voltage. The catalog block is therefore c_rating, connector and cell_class — the three things a builder actually narrows a shelf of packs by, and none of which any model reads. 'nominal_v' is the pack's RESTING voltage at full charge in this model, which is the datum the state-of-charge term measures its fall from; see physics.md §5. Entries are ordered by cell count and then capacity, which is what gives the cell filter an ascending order without anything sorting it.
